name: Meridian Municipal Supply AG-7 'Hotstock'
description:
The Meridian Municipal Supply AG-7 is an agricultural cattle prod, manufactured for livestock management in the urban farming cooperatives and vertical ranching operations that supply GLMZ's food chain. It is a 90-centimeter fiberglass-and-ABS rod with a two-prong stainless steel contact at the tip, designed to deliver a sharp, brief shock to the flank of a large animal — sufficient to redirect behavior without causing lasting harm to the animal or its market value. It runs on two standard D-cell battery equivalents, has no charging port, no digital components, and no safety mechanism beyond a simple sliding power switch. It costs Φ15 at any agricultural supply outlet and is available without any documentation whatsoever.

The AG-7 was never designed as a weapon. It was designed to move cattle through chutes. That it has become one of the most common improvised defensive and offensive tools in Tier 1 and lower Tier 2 is a testament to the gap between what people can afford and what the formal weapons market provides. The shock output is lower than dedicated security batons — approximately 30,000 volts at very low amperage — and the contact range is shorter, but it is immediate, it is reliable, and it leaves no purchase record that flags a personal protection permit database.

Meridian Municipal Supply has periodically faced pressure from municipal security contractors to add purchase restrictions or tracking to AG-7 units, given their prevalence at crime scenes. The company has consistently and successfully argued that the AG-7 is a farm tool and that restricting it would harm legitimate agricultural operations in the city's food-production districts. This argument is legally sound and practically convenient for everyone involved.
legality: Legal — classified as agricultural equipment; no permit, registration, or documentation required for purchase
specifications: Length: 900mm Weight: 480g Discharge Voltage: ~30,000V Amperage: 0.001A (fixed) Power Source: 2x D-cell battery equivalent (replaceable) Battery Life: ~200 activations Contact Type: Dual stainless steel prong Body: ABS/fiberglass composite Safety: Sliding power switch only Price: Φ15
tactical_use: In agricultural use, the AG-7 is pressed firmly against the flank of an animal and the trigger button depressed for a half-second burst. In improvised defensive use, the same technique applies to human targets — it requires solid contact to be effective, meaning the user must be within arm's reach. The weapon's length gives it modest reach advantage over a fist. Its effectiveness against augmented individuals varies widely; those with significant subdermal plating or insulating chrome may feel little effect. On unaugmented or lightly augmented targets, the shock causes a brief, sharp muscular response that is more startling than incapacitating.
cultural_context: In Tier 1, the AG-7 is simply 'the prod' or 'farmer's friend,' and carrying one openly in certain districts is understood as a quiet statement about economic reality rather than agricultural occupation. There is no shame in it and no pretense — it is what it is, a Φ15 piece of hardware that might save your life or might not, and everyone knows the difference between it and a real security baton. Some Tier 1 community defense groups have begun spray-painting their prods in identifying colors to signal affiliation and mutual-aid membership.
known_users: vertical ranch and urban farm workers
community defense patrols in unpoliced districts
story_hooks: A batch of AG-7 units from a specific manufacturing run have been quietly modified during distribution — a micro-component soldered into the discharge circuit that triples output voltage, enough to be genuinely dangerous. Someone is arming a specific neighborhood, and the question is whether they're protecting it or preparing it for something.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian cattle prod: a long, straight fiberglass rod tapering slightly toward a dual-pronged steel contact tip. Inelegant and purely functional. No aesthetic concession whatsoever. Looks like exactly what it is — a farm tool that happens to deliver electrical shock.
physical_description.dimensions: 90cm total length; 2.5cm diameter at grip; dual-prong contact spread 3cm apart
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight and well-balanced; feels substantial enough to have heft but not fatiguing to hold or swing. Approximately 480g distributed evenly along the rod.
physical_description.primary_material: Fiberglass composite rod core wrapped in rigid ABS plastic casing
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial finish — no gloss, minimal reflection. Scuffed and slightly yellowed from sun exposure and field use. Weathered rather than worn.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pale cream or off-white ABS body with stainless steel prong contact at the tip. Battery compartment at grip end is darker plastic, often with faded Meridian Municipal Supply branding.
physical_description.grip_texture: Slightly textured ABS plastic with no intentional gripping aid — plain, rough enough to prevent slipping, cold to the touch
distinctive_features: Dual stainless steel contact prongs at the tip, spread slightly and dulled from repeated use
Simple sliding power switch near the grip — no LED indicators or feedback lights
Exposed battery compartment cap at the base (removable via coin or tool)
Faint manufacturing seams running the length of the rod
No safety guard, no wrist loop, no decorative elements
Fine hairline cracks in the ABS finish on most units, especially near the grip
Contact prongs often darkened with oxidation despite stainless steel
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Meridian Municipal Supply AG-7 stamped in raised text along the upper third of the rod. Serial numbers and regulatory marks in tiny print near the battery cap. No logos beyond the manufacturer name.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but functional. Minor cosmetic damage expected. Contact prongs show oxidation. ABS casing may be cracked or discolored. Battery compartment cap often scratched from repeated access. Never pristine; always serviceable.
